cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. This dripping tap is our chance to replace the whole sink. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Excellent. We'll fit it while the sink's out and replace that swollen worktop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll empty the kitchen. With the cupboards out, we can finally fix the layout.

mechanism: A confidently manages a tap repair by adopting B small solution but expanding the job around every constraint, conceding design preferences to keep B involved.
confusable: Unlike simple efficiency or fixing the stated fault, each reply expands disruption; authority must accommodate B participation without shrinking the scope.
comparison: Domestic washer/worktop/cupboards chain differs from a cafe wobble becoming floor and service renovation.
seedUse: Use D48-a purchased washer/swollen worktop/cupboard dependency and S02-a claiming an adopted suggestion as part of a broader plan.
